builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
summary: CurvDelta replaces standard fine-tuning or LoRA update parameterization with updates projected into a low-curvature subspace (via K-FAC approximate curvature and a factorized projection, plus a CurvLoRA variant) so that adaptation leaves the pre-adaptation model's preservation loss nearly invariant. It costs extra computation and implementation complexity for K-FAC curvature estimation and projection at training time, and K-FAC itself adds memory and per-step overhead relative to plain LoRA, though inference cost is unchanged. It can fail if the local quadratic curvature approximation does not hold over the full update trajectory, in which case capability degradation returns, or if the preservation gains do not exceed those of cheaper alternatives such as KL-regularized or low-learning-rate LoRA.
rationale: The method is implementable on a single GPU as a fine-tuning-time modification, but its acquisition-retention advantage is qualitative and must be validated against simpler baselines such as LoRA with regularization on the reader's own task.

claims.statement: CurvDelta replaces standard fine-tuning or LoRA update parameterization with updates projected into a low-curvature subspace (via K-FAC approximate curvature and a factorized projection, plus a CurvLoRA variant) so that adaptation leaves the pre-adaptation model's preservation loss nearly invariant. It costs extra computation and implementation complexity for K-FAC curvature estimation and projection at training time, and K-FAC itself adds memory and per-step overhead relative to plain LoRA, though inference cost is unchanged. It can fail if the local quadratic curvature approximation does not hold over the full update trajectory, in which case capability degradation returns, or if the preservation gains do not exceed those of cheaper alternatives such as KL-regularized or low-learning-rate LoRA.

Competitive downstream performance on math reasoning and code generation with better general-capability preservation than baselines; on TOFU and MUSE unlearning, better forgetting-retention balance with retention close to from-scratch retraining. No multiplicative factor stated.
